picks.title: I Used AI to Write & Publish a Book in 30 Days (Here's What Happened...)
picks.excerpt: Bestselling author Scott Allan walks through the exact framework used to write, edit and publish a complete nonfiction manuscript in 30 days with Claude, including where the human editing pass was non-negotiable.
picks.rationale: Most actionable item in the pool — a named author's end-to-end Claude manuscript workflow with the human-editing checkpoints spelled out.

picks.title: 7 Mistakes That Scream "AI TEXT" (and How to Fix It)
picks.excerpt: A craft-level breakdown of the seven tells that mark prose as machine-written, and line-edit fixes for each. Useful for the current wave of AI-detection disputes hitting authors and agents.
picks.rationale: Concrete line-edit fixes for the tells that get manuscripts flagged as machine-written — directly changes how you finish AI-assisted prose.

picks.title: European Union's AI Act requires transparency around specific types of AI-generated content
picks.excerpt: The EU AI Act's transparency obligations cover AI-generated or AI-manipulated content that could be mistaken as real, pushing disclosure and labelling from a voluntary courtesy toward a compliance requirement for anyone publishing AI-assisted work into the EU.
picks.rationale: Turns AI disclosure from etiquette into a compliance requirement for anyone selling AI-assisted books into the EU.

picks.title: How to Get Barnes & Noble to Host Your Book Signing | Self-Publishing News (August 6, 2026)
picks.excerpt: This week's indie-author news covers ProWritingAid's new ProWritingMethod editing system plus platform updates from Apple Books, Lulu and Voices by INAudio, alongside Barnes & Noble tightening its local author-event rules.
picks.rationale: Freshest tool news in the section — ProWritingAid's new ProWritingMethod plus Apple Books, Lulu and INAudio platform changes in one pass.

picks.title: AI May Be Making Publishing Easier, But It's Still Not Easy
picks.excerpt: At the Media Transformation Summit cohosted by Publishing Signal, speakers agreed AI is accelerating production and lowering costs, but curation, audience-finding and judgement calls remain stubbornly human. One thread: AI systems favour content with explicit, machine-friendly structure, so publishers may have to rewrite how they present plot summaries, author bios and images online.
picks.rationale: Highest-credibility trade read, with one usable takeaway: AI surfaces favour explicitly structured metadata, so blurbs and bios need rewriting for machines.
